title: Stop Making Models Bigger, Make Them Behave — Kobie Crawford, Snorkel
talk_summary: Snorkel and UC Berkeley's RLLM team fine-tuned a 4B-parameter model with GRPO on a curated, expert-verified FinQA tool-use dataset, and it beat a 235B model on financial tool-use tasks. The key finding is that the small model's failure mode was tool discipline (discovering tables, inspecting schemas, self-correcting on errors), not reasoning, and that fixing that one behavior generalized to harder multi-table questions.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a single pass/fail score, they break correctness into a list of sub-questions (a rubric) so they can localize which specific behavior is failing, then target data/prompting at that behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: building rubrics as part of our evals... breaking down the rightness or wrongness of a model's response into a full list of different questions

takeaways.what_they_do: The winning behavior was procedural: call get_table_names, then get_table_info, then query, then self-correct on error. The big model had the tools but skipped discovery and hallucinated.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the first thing it did was actually query to find out what tables it had available to it
takeaways.numbers: 4B model roughly doubled pass@1 vs its prior baseline and beat the 235B model

takeaways.technique: Small model + behavior tuning over big model
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue against defaulting to a larger model when the real gap is behavioral, and show a small model with the right data/behavior can match or beat a much larger one on a constrained task.
takeaways.numbers: 4B beat 235B; training run ~21 hours, under $500 per run

takeaways.technique: Target the single core failure mode
takeaways.what_they_do: They isolated one failure mode (tool use) and fixed only that; the fix generalized to harder unseen tasks rather than needing broader training.
takeaways.evidence_quote: given that core failure mode being fixed, it turned out that that then made the model better... generalizing to other question sets
takeaways.numbers: Multi-table benchmark jumped 13.9% to 26.6% after single-table-only training

takeaways.what_they_do: Before training/eval they verify each task has a checkable ground-truth answer and that the environment is self-contained with no external dependencies.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we should be able to have a verifiable answer that we're looking for
